paragraphs: R' Reuven Ha-Itarbuli. Avot De-Rabbi Natan, chapter 16. Once the government decreed that they must not observe Shabbat or circumcise their sons, and must have intercourse with menstruants. He went and cut his hair komi-style (shaving it like a forelock so that they would not recognize him as a Jew). He asked them, ‘Should one who has an enemy make him poor or rich?’ They answered, ‘Poor.’ He told them, ‘Let him not do work on Shabbat,’ and they rescinded the decree, etc. They recognized that he was a Jew and reinstated it. They sent R' Shimon ben Yohai and R' Elazar bar R' Yosi to Rome, and they annulled the decree (see there): Me'ilah 17a:11–15 and 17b:6. He wished to be killed in place of R' Yehudah ben Bava (see there). Mo'ed Katan 18b: ‘Rav said in R' Reuven's name,’ etc.; Rav said in his name, etc.; some say, ‘It was taught in a baraita in the name of R' Reuven ben Itztrobili.’ Although he preceded Rav by much, we find later figures speaking in earlier figures' names; or Rav is R' Abba, R' Shimon ben Yohai's pupil. His two sons were Rabbi's pupils. He [the observer is unstated] saw the Angel of Death looking at them and grinding his teeth. He said, ‘Let us exile them to the south; perhaps exile atones.’ The Angel of Death went and took them from there [the subject follows from the parallel narrative]. Jerusalem Talmud, end of Kilayim, halakhah 4 [9:3:14 in the checked edition], and Ketubbot, end of Ha-Nose [12:3:14]. His burial is in Aravya (see R' Hanina ben Dosa).
